name: DigitalOcean
description: DigitalOcean rents out cloud computing to small and mid-sized technology businesses, developers and, increasingly, AI companies: virtual servers (Droplets), storage, managed databases and Kubernetes, managed WordPress-style hosting (Cloudways) and GPU servers and AI agent tools (Gradient, built on the Paperspace acquisition). Customers mostly pay by monthly usage with simple, predictable pricing and sign up on the website without a sales call; a growing minority commit to a minimum spend. Revenue grew 15 percent to $901.4 million in FY2025 and 29 percent in Q2 2026, with AI customers (those using any AI/ML product) now $234 million of the $1,125 million annual run rate. Growth is now being bought with heavy data-center and GPU spending: gross margin fell from 60 to 55 percent in Q2 2026 and the top 25 customers rose from 9 to 20 percent of revenue.

gics.note: Listed in the S&P MidCap 400 with sector Information Technology and sub-industry Internet Services & Infrastructure (Wikipedia 'List of S&P 400 companies', raw wikitext read 2026-10-27). That page gives only sector and sub-industry; industry group and industry left null rather than recalled from memory.

businessLines.name: Digital Native Enterprise customers (spend above $500 a month)
businessLines.how: Usage-based monthly bills for compute, storage, bandwidth and managed services, mostly month-to-month; some customers sign committed minimum-spend contracts (remaining performance obligations $134.1M at 2025-12-31, weighted life 2.0 years).
businessLines.description: About 21,736 customers (Q2 2026 average) of which 632 spend over $100K a year-equivalent, 92 over $500K and 45 over $1M.

revenue.note: FY2025 10-K Note 3. Q2 2026 DNE share of revenue 67% (59% a year earlier), DNE revenue +45% YoY (Q2 2026 10-Q).

businessLines.revenueNote: FY2025 10-K Note 3. Q2 2026 DNE share of revenue 67% (59% a year earlier), DNE revenue +45% YoY (Q2 2026 10-Q).

businessLines.name: Developers and other (spend $500 or less a month, legacy Bare Metal CPU, miscellaneous)
businessLines.how: Pay-as-you-go monthly usage billed by credit card from the self-service website; low acquisition cost, higher churn risk.
businessLines.description: Roughly 155,000 small accounts under the old naming (Builders spending $50 to $500) plus smaller testers.

businessLines.name: AI customers (any customer using an AI/ML product, with their other cloud spend)
businessLines.how: Rents GPU time by the hour or on committed contracts, plus token and agent usage on the Gradient platform; the cost is heavy up-front GPU and data center spend, which is why gross margin has dropped.
businessLines.description: Customers using GPU Droplets, Bare Metal GPUs or the Gradient AI platform and agents.
businessLines.revenueNote: AI/ML product revenue alone is not disclosed. AI Customer ARR (latest quarter revenue times four, including these customers' non-AI usage) was $234M at 2026-06-30 vs $75M at 2025-06-30 (Q2 2026 10-Q), about 21% of total ARR of $1,125M (derived).

businessLines.name: Managed Hosting (Cloudways) and PaaS/SaaS (managed databases, Kubernetes, App Platform)
businessLines.how: Monthly fee that bundles infrastructure with management and support, higher price per unit of compute than raw Droplets.
businessLines.description: Managed hosting for agencies, bloggers and e-commerce sites on WordPress, PHP and Magento; fully managed databases, container and serverless services.

brands.name: DigitalOcean (Droplets, Spaces, Managed Kubernetes and Databases, App Platform)
brands.share: Core platform; revenue by product not disclosed

brands.share: AI Customer ARR $234M of $1,125M total ARR at 2026-06-30 (about 21%, includes these customers' non-AI usage)
